newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends higher on supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends higher on supply concerns.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline prices hit six- month highs Monday but ended only marginally higher after supply concerns generated by refinery problems abated.
"The problem with the Amoco refinery is probably not that bad," said Rita Beale, an analyst with Fimat USA Futures.

November gasoline ended up 0.20 cent at 70.30 cents a gallon after prices rose to a six-month high and a contract high of 71.75 cents a gallon. November heating oil ended off 0.26 cent at 71.46 cents gallon while December crude settled off one cent a barrel at $24.85.

"People were looking for a reason to sell heating oil and buy gasoline, and the refinery problems were a convenient excuse," said Michael Rothman, senior energy futures analyst at Merrill Lynch. Crude followed the oil complex lower, traders said.
Environmental regulators said a valve failure caused an operation upset of a gasoline making unit at Amoco Corp's 433,000 barrel per day (bpd) Texas City, Texas refinery.
There was also talk that a 40,000 bpd gasoline making unit at Chevron Corp's Pascagoula, Mississippi refinery was shut down for seasonal maintenance. Chevron declined comment.

Meanwhile, Lagoven, an affiliate of Petroleos de Venezuala, said the 108,000 bpd catalytic cracker at its Amuay refinery in Venezuala would be back online in three weeks after being shut due to problems with its compressor.
The Lagoven news combined with views that Amoco's refinery problems were minimal weighed on oil prices late session, traders said.
Lagoven reiterated that it would be able to meet supply contracts despite the shutdown.
"The market turned south on a combination of refinery news," said a trader.
-- Harry Milling, New York Enery Desk, 212-859-1761
